bugs.fix: <meta name="description" content="A concise description under 160 characters for search results.">
bugs.explanation: The meta description appears in search results below the page title. Without it, search engines generate one from page content (often poorly). Write a unique, compelling description under 160 characters for each page.

bugs.fix:
<meta property="og:title" content="My Article">
  <meta property="og:description" content="Article description here">
  <meta property="og:image" content="https://example.com/image.jpg">
  <meta property="og:url" content="https://example.com/article">
bugs.explanation: Open Graph meta tags control how pages appear when shared on social media. Without them, platforms use their own (often incorrect) extraction. Add `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:image`, and `og:url` at minimum.

When the same content is accessible at multiple URLs (with/without trailing slash, with parameters), duplicate content confuses search engines. Use `<link rel="canonical">` to identify the preferred URL, consolidating SEO value.

Structured data (JSON-LD with Schema.org vocabulary) enables rich results in search engines (recipe cards, FAQs, breadcrumbs, etc.). Adding appropriate schema markup can dramatically improve click-through rates from search results.

title: hreflang for Multi-language
code:
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="en" href="https://example.com/en/">
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="fr" href="https://example.com/fr/">
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="x-default" href="https://example.com/">

bugs.explanation: Breadcrumbs should use `<ol>` (ordered list, as they have sequence) with `aria-label="Breadcrumb"` on the `<nav>`. The current page item should use `aria-current="page"` rather than being a link.

bugs.fix: 1 2 3
bugs.explanation: Wrap pagination in `<nav aria-label="Pagination">`. Add `aria-label="Page N"` to each link so screen readers announce meaningful names instead of just numbers. Mark the current page with `aria-current="page"`.

bugs.fix:
<!-- Use HTTP 301 redirect on the server instead -->
<!-- Or JavaScript: window.location.replace('https://example.com/new') -->
bugs.explanation: `<meta http-equiv="refresh">` for redirects is discouraged — it doesn't send the correct HTTP status code, hurts SEO (no PageRank transfer), confuses screen readers, and can be disorienting. Use a server-side 301 redirect instead.

bugs.fix:
<link rel="icon" href="/favicon.ico" sizes="any">
<link rel="icon" href="/favicon.svg" type="image/svg+xml">
<link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="/apple-touch-icon.png">
bugs.explanation: Modern browsers prefer SVG favicons (scalable, supports dark mode). Add an SVG favicon alongside the `.ico` fallback, plus `apple-touch-icon` for iOS home screen icons.
A web app manifest enables PWA features (installability, splash screen, theme color). Add `<link rel="manifest">` and `<meta name="theme-color">` to make your web app installable on mobile devices.

`async` downloads the script asynchronously and executes immediately on load (good for independent scripts like analytics). `defer` downloads asynchronously and executes in order after HTML parsing (good for scripts that depend on DOM or each other).

bugs.fix:
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Roboto">
bugs.explanation: `rel="preconnect"` establishes a connection (DNS + TCP + TLS) to a third-party origin early, reducing latency when the browser later fetches resources from it. Add it before external font or CDN resource links.

bugs.fix: Please enable JavaScript to use this app.
bugs.explanation: `<noscript>` provides fallback content when JavaScript is disabled. Even if your app requires JS, inform users why they see a blank page rather than leaving them confused.

The `<template>` element holds HTML that is not rendered but can be cloned by JavaScript. It's better than `display:none` because its content is completely inert (no images loaded, no scripts executed) until cloned into the document.

Use `<slot>` elements in web component templates to define insertion points for projected content. Named slots (`name="title"`) allow consumers to target specific placeholders; unnamed slots receive any unmatched content.
Using `type="email"` instead of `type="text"` adds browser-native validation (format check), shows an email keyboard on mobile (with @ symbol), and enables proper autocomplete behavior.

`type="number"` is for numeric values that can be incremented (ages, quantities). For phone numbers, use `type="tel"` which shows the telephone keyboard on mobile without the spin controls. Add `pattern` for format validation.

bugs.fix:
<form id="signup" novalidate>
  <!-- Prevents browser's native validation UI so you can provide custom validation messages -->
bugs.explanation: Browser native form validation (`required`, `type`, `pattern`) shows inconsistent UI across browsers and can't be styled. Adding `novalidate` disables it so you can implement consistent, accessible custom validation with better error messages.

`enterkeyhint` tells mobile keyboards what label to show on the Enter key ("search", "go", "done", "send", "next", "previous"). Using `enterkeyhint="search"` shows a magnifying glass, improving the mobile form experience.
